verdict.rationale: Convex ships an official MCP server exposing deployment-management tools to AI agents, documents 'agent-setup' guidance, and explicitly says it 'works great with coding agents' for creating apps from natural-language prompts; a hands-on probe confirms the MCP server's stdio handshake actually works keylessly. However, this NL operability is mediated entirely through third-party coding agents/IDEs via MCP rather than a built-in NL command interface, and there's no evidence of the breadth of commands agents can reliably issue in practice. Missing for 10: end-to-end example of an NL command executing a real deployment action, independent user reports of NL-driven operation, and any built-in first-party chat/NL layer beyond MCP.
